interpretation: Source fact: a g-deformation diagram augments a differential graded Lie algebra A by evaluation ε:A⁰→g, records finite-dimensionality in cohomology, and calls the diagram rigid when H⁰→g is injective. interpretation: Source fact: for an Artinian base S with nilpotent maximal ideal, deformations are Maurer–Cartan elements η∈A¹⊗m satisfying dη+½[η,η]=0 together with frame data in the identity neighborhood of G, modulo the exponential action of A⁰⊗m. For a rigid finite-dimensional diagram this quotient functor is prorepresented by R(A,ε). In the framed principal Higgs, de Rham, and Betti cases, R(A,ε) is naturally the formal completion of the corresponding representation space. Morphisms of diagrams induce maps of formal deformation spaces, and the stated quasi-isomorphisms induce isomorphisms. Interpretive inference: the formal neighborhood is recovered by solving one universal nonlinear compatibility equation order by order and dividing by infinitesimal gauge, while quasi-isomorphism discards chain-level choices without discarding first-order directions or possible obstructions.
nonparaphrase_operation: Probe a moduli point by every nilpotent Artinian thickening, encode each lift as a Maurer–Cartan solution plus frame displacement, quotient by exponentiated degree-zero gauge, and replace the original complex by any diagram with identical H⁰/H¹ and no loss of H² obstructions.

boundary_or_failure: The proof is specialized to GL(n)-representation spaces of a compact Riemann surface, with the stated main theorem assuming a smooth projective curve of genus greater than two and the argument separately treating the exceptional genus-two, rank-two codimension case. interpretation: Source fact: the Betti representation space is the fiber of the single surface relation in GL(n)^{2g}, giving a component-dimension lower bound. Irreducible representations form a smooth locus of the expected dimension. Reducible representations are covered by conjugates of block parabolics; induction on the diagonal ranks and cohomology of the off-diagonal block bound this locus, showing that every component meets the irreducible locus and that the singular locus has codimension at least two, including a direct tangent calculation in the exceptional case. Being a complete intersection supplies Cohen–Macaulay S2, while codimension-one smoothness supplies R1, hence normality by Serre. Isosingularity transfers normality to de Rham and Dolbeault representation spaces, and invariant-ring quotients preserve it for coarse moduli. Interpretive inference: normality is obtained by isolating the only plausible bad locus through representation type, proving it too small to affect codimension one, and then using local-model equivalence instead of repeating the singularity analysis in every realization.
nonparaphrase_operation: Present representations as a one-relation fiber, stratify the reducible locus by invariant-subspace dimension via parabolic subgroups, estimate each stratum through its diagonal representations and off-diagonal group cohomology, combine complete-intersection S2 with codimension-one regularity, and transport the resulting local property through isosingularity and good quotients.

boundary_or_failure: The abstract connectedness criterion needs an algebraic C* action on a quasiprojective variety, a linearized ample bundle, existence of zero-limits for every point, and a connected fixed subset U. Its application is specific to degree-zero Higgs bundles on a smooth projective curve: the deformation of a nonunitary fixed point uses a Hodge-bundle decomposition, Riemann–Roch, openness of stability, and connectedness of the vector-bundle moduli locus. Connectedness upgrades to irreducibility only after normality has already been proved.
interpretation: Source fact: a linearized projective embedding assigns weights to fixed components, and any nonconstant C* orbit has strictly ordered weights at its two limits. If every fixed point outside a connected core U is the infinity-limit of a nonconstant orbit, a hypothetical disjoint component would contain a fixed point of minimal zero-limit weight and the incoming orbit would force a still smaller one, a contradiction. For a fixed stable Higgs bundle with nonzero Higgs field, the Hodge decomposition has negative- and positive-degree extreme pieces; a nontrivial extension between them produces a different stable Higgs bundle whose scaled limit is the original. Applying this componentwise to a polystable fixed point and taking U to be the connected zero-Higgs locus proves connectedness. Interpretive inference: the proof rules out extra components by orienting degenerations toward every fixed stratum outside one connected core, rather than by constructing paths between arbitrary points.
nonparaphrase_operation: Linearize the C* action to order fixed strata by weights; in any alleged component disjoint from U, choose a minimal-weight fixed point and contradict minimality using a nonconstant orbit flowing into it. Construct the required incoming orbit concretely by deforming the extension between the extreme Hodge summands of a fixed Higgs bundle.
source_support: Lemma 11.8 proves the minimal-weight connectedness criterion from projective weight decompositions. Lemma 11.9 constructs the extension family F_t for a stable fixed Higgs bundle with nonzero field and proves F_1 is not isomorphic to the limit object. Corollary 11.10 applies the criterion to the connected zero-Higgs/vector-bundle locus and direct sums of stable components. The final theorem combines transferred connectedness with prior normality to obtain irreducibility.
